item.title: Agentic Organizations: Designing, Governing, and Managing AI Agents
item.content:encoded:
Martin Adam, University of Goettingen

Aaron Baird, Colorado State University

Mari-Klara Stein, Tallinn University of Technology

Alexander Benlian, Technical University of Darmstadt

AI is transitioning from a tool for individual productivity assistance to a participant in organizational action through agentic systems that can interpret goals, perceive states, plan actions, and execute tasks with autonomy. This shift reconfigures organizational arrangements, requiring new thinking about delegation, accountability, control, and oversight.

Agentic organizations embed AI agents within routines, systems, and workflows, creating sociotechnical arrangements impacting core operational systems. Information systems scholars are well-positioned to address this transition given existing expertise in organizational change, algorithmic management, platform governance, and human-AI collaboration.

This special issue seeks research on how organizations can design, govern, and manage human-AI ensembles while preserving accountability, resilience, and human judgment. Papers should examine delegated agentic participation in organizational action, including governance mechanisms, workflow redesign, multi-agent systems, epistemic challenges, workforce implications, and safety considerations.

Appel publié par Journal of Management Information Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Delegated autonomy and control in agentic organizations
  • Accountability and oversight mechanisms for AI agents
  • Agentic process redesign and workflow transformation
  • Organizational capability building for agentic systems
  • Multi-agent orchestration and coordination
  • Agent interoperability and digital ecosystems
  • Epistemic governance and trust in AI agents
  • Opacity and contestability of AI-generated actions
  • Cognitive and behavioral implications of agentic AI
  • Workforce implications and professional identity
  • Skill formation and reliance on AI agents
  • Resilience and safety in agentic systems
  • Security and compliance in agentic workflows
  • Societal consequences and ethical implications of agentic AI
  • Human-AI ensembles and human authority preservation
